description.narrative: The objective of the Rural Competitiveness Project (COMRURAL) for Honduras is to contribute to increased productivity and competitiveness among organized rural small-scale producers through their participation in productive alliances. There are three components to the project. The first component is the support to productive alliances. It will support pre-investment activities to: (i) promote the project concept and outreach to the Rural Producer Organizations (RPOs), commercial partners and private financing entities; (ii) create and consolidate productive alliances among RPOs and commercial partners; (iii) identify potential business opportunities, including, inter alia, opportunities with respect to basic grains, on the part of the productive alliance; (iv) fully prepare the business opportunity into a business plan; and (v) build capacity among technical service providers to enhance the quality of their services provided to the productive alliances. The second component is the productive investments. It will provide subproject grants to co-finance the implementation of approximately 150 feasible business plans formulated under first component. In order to become eligible, a business plan must be financially feasible, entail a concrete productive alliance, and have secured up-front resources from the private financial sector (minimum of 30 percent) to support the business plan. Finally, the third component is the project coordination, monitoring, and evaluation. It will support the incremental costs associated with the project administration, monitoring, including the setting up and implementation of a participatory monitoring and evaluation system.

The revised PDO is (a) to contribute to increased productivity and competitiveness among organized rural small-scale producers through their participation in productive alliances and (b) to enable the Government to respond promptly and effectively to an eligible emergency.

comment.narrative:
<p>Exceeded.  119% of target</p>

<p>This indicator measures the members from the 163 alliances that were financed under the Project.</p>

<p>This includes 7132 beneficiaries under the original credit and 5746 beneficiaries under the new financing following the AF.</p>

<p> </p>

title.narrative: Number of productive alliances under implementation

comment.narrative:
<p>Substantially met.  86% of target</p>

<p> </p>

<p>This indicator measures the number of productive alliances that the Project financed. A productive alliance under the Project included an RPO, a commercial partner, a PFI, and a technical service provider. Occasionally a single business plan could include more than one RPO and these were counted as separate productive alliances since the definition of the productive alliance was met. (The PAD explicitly differentiates between business plans and productive alliances)</p>

<p>122 productive alliances were financed in the first round and 41 after the AF</p>

title.narrative: Percentage increase in land and labor productivity by rural producers participating in the project

comment.narrative:
<p>Exceeded.  118% of target</p>

<p>The wording of the indicator was meant to be modified to include only land productivity (labor productivity was deemed to be too complicated to calculate). Therefore the calculated indicator only accounts for land productivity</p>

<p>Amount of crop production was taken to be the indicator for land productivity.</p>

<p>Increase in yield was calculated for each value chain and then averaged for each value chain</p>

<p>The increase in land productivity was 24% for plans financed before the AF and 23% after the AF </p>

title.narrative: Number of rural producer organizations have produced a profile that is approved to become a business plan.

comment.narrative:
<p>Met.  100% of target</p>

<p>This indicator measures the number of RPOs whose profiles were approved by the evaluation committee as having an eligible business plan for financing.</p>

<p>However not all of these were financed because of various reasons a key one was that not all of them could secure financing from PFIs.</p>

title.narrative: Percentage increase in the value of gross sales of the rural producer organizations based on implementation of the business plan.

comment.narrative:
<p>Exceeded.  255% of target</p>

<p>The baseline value for sales is taken for all the OPRSand the sales value at the closing is taken (adjusted for inflation with index from the Honduras Central Bank). The final indicator is calculated by the (∑Result / ∑Baseline) -1.</p>

<p>The increase in sales was 23% for plans financed in the first phase of the Project and 28% in the second phase of the Project. We take the average of these values.</p>

<p>Sales data was recorded for each OPR annually</p>

<p>Exceeded.  138% of target???????</p>
<p>A total amount of US$34 million was raised by the Project out of which US$20.5 Million was raised through the private financial institutions and US$13.5 Million that was raised through the finances of the RPOs</p>

title.narrative: Number of technical service providers are approved to provide support to rural producer organizations

comment.narrative:
<p>Exceeded.  118% of target</p>

<p> </p>

<p>51 PSDEs (37 private institutions approved PSDEs and 14 individual consultants (PSDEs)) provided support for the alliances before the AF and an additional 12 new service providers were registered following the AF</p>

title.narrative: Targeted clients satisfied with agricultural services (percentage)

comment.narrative:
<p>Exceeded.  105% of target</p>

<p>???????</p>

<p>This is based on a survey measuring self-reported satisfaction with project services.</p>

<p> </p>

<p>Later disaggregated values state the number of beneficiaries who should have been targeted for the survey and how many responded as being satisfied with the survey.</p>

title.narrative: Percentage of business plans financed by the project are implemented using good environmental practices

comment.narrative:
<p>Exceeded.  128% of target</p>

<p>The indicator was calculated based on RPOs adopting applicable "good" environmental practices in the implementation of their business plans. </p>

<p>Specific practices were agreed upon with assistance fromthe technical service provider which were specific to each business plan. They were divided into 5 sub-categories which included</p>

<p>i) Management of water including efficient irrigation practices such as drip irrigation or recycle water generated as a waste from washing utensils or other materials ii) Management of solid waste for example  adoption of dry recycling (use of coffee husks as fuel) ii) Environmental licenses-COMRURAL project requires each OPR to obtain an environmental permit from the Ministry of the Environment,iv) GAP-soil analysis to assess the level of nutrients contained in the soil, periodic and deep cleaning of weeds, reforestation of sources and water-producing areas, the catchment of CO2 through the conservation of forest areas, reforestation with agroforestry systems, pest control through traps and the planting of fruit trees and v) Environmental Certifications.  </p>

<p>The TSP reported to the PIU whether the RPO was following the steps laid out in the business plan</p>

title.narrative: Percentage of rural producer organizations that are working under an alliance approach 24 months after first disbursement

comment.narrative:
<p>Exceeded.  118% of target</p>

<p>This indicator was introduced with the restructuring and additional financing in May 2017and is therefore measured only for the alliances formed after the additional financing</p>

<p>This indicator measures if the alliance is still sustained 2 years after the first disbursements so before the closing of the business plan implementation under the Project which is planned for 3 years</p>

<p> </p>

title.narrative: Percentage of investments identified in the business plans are completed on schedule

comment.narrative:
<p>Exceeded.  121% of target</p>

<p> </p>

<p>This indicator measures if the outline for implementation of the business plan followed was implemented as laid out.</p>

<p>Occasionally RPOs requested a change in the timeline of investments and these were formally included in the proposal. These are not counted as implementation being off schedule</p>

title.narrative: Percentage of business plans in the project successfully implement measures that target the youth and indigenous communities,when applicable, as identified in the business plan.

comment.narrative:
<p>Exceeded.  139% of target</p>

<p> </p>

<p>This indicator includes RPOs that adopted specific measures that increasedthe participation of youth and Indigenous communities in the RPOs. Each RPO initially outlined the steps that they would take to follow the procedures to increase inclusivity. The specific steps included training and specific targets to increase the numbers in the RPO as members or in the Indigenous organizations.</p>

<p>The TSP reported to the PIU whether the RPO was following the steps laid out in the business plan</p>

title.narrative: MIS fully functional and producing all required products

comment.narrative:
<p>Indicator met.</p>
<p>The MIS was deemed to be fully functional in 2015</p>

<p>The indicator target was met.</p>
<p>Financial audits were deemed satisfactory</p>

title.narrative: By the end of the Project, at least 120 productive alliances under implementation

comment.narrative: Achieved. 123 RPOs implemented 89 business plans. The target was reduced after partial cancellation.

title.narrative: 175 RPOs have produced a profile that is approved to become a business plan

comment.narrative: Not achieved. Target was reduced after partial cancellation.

title.narrative: 10% increase in the value of gross sales of the RPOs based on the implementation of the business plan

comment.narrative: Exceeded. The original indicator was redefined, which was "annual sales/income increase of RPOs under productive alliances increase by 10 percent". The actual value achieved is an average increase in gross sales between coffee RPOs (27%) and veg RPO (11%)

title.narrative: At least 15 technical service providers (TSP) are approved to provide support to RPO

comment.narrative: Exceeded. 51 TSPs were approved by the project. However, 13 of them were active as of end-2016. The original indicator was redefined, which was "at least 15 TSP are certified".

title.narrative: Private actors investment as loans to producer organizations represent at least 50% of the amount invested as grant by the public sector

comment.narrative: Surpassed. The original indicator was redefined, which was "US$ 12.05 million co-invested in business plans by private financial sector". These actors invested more than 50% of the business plans, which amounted to US$ 13.9 million.

title.narrative: By the end of the Project, at least 5,280 rural producers have benefited from Project financing

comment.narrative: Exceeded. 7,200 rural producers had membership in project-supported RPOs, which exceeded even the original targets. 28 percent of the RPO members were women.

title.narrative: 85% satisfaction among RPOs regarding technical assistance from service providers (TSP)

comment.narrative: Not achieved. Not all project-approved TSPs performed satisfactorily. As of end-2016, only 13 out of 51 approved TSPs were active.

title.narrative: At least 80% of the producers with approved business plans are satisfied with the project

comment.narrative: Not achieved. Some RPOs were not satisfied with slow fund transfer from the project or quality of technical support by service providers.

title.narrative: At least 150 business plans approved for financing

comment.narrative: Dropped after July 2011 restructuring and moved to IO Indicator 5 (Component 2)

title.narrative: At least 70% of participating RPOs receive project financing business plan

comment.narrative: Instead, this was measured by two intermediate outcome indicators. The target was surpassed, as 77% of RPOs which produced business profiles received project financing.

title.narrative: At least 200 quality business plans proposed with project support

comment.narrative: Measured in the Intermediate Outcome Indicator 1.

title.narrative: At least 40 percent increase in net revenues for the participating RPOs via the productive alliances

comment.narrative: PDO indicators redefined. The increase in competitiveness was measured by gross sales (PDO Indicator 3).

title.narrative: RPOs profit margin increased at least 15% in real terms

comment.narrative: PDO indicators redefined. The increase in competitiveness was measured by gross sales (PDO Indicator 3).

title.narrative: Unit production cost of RPOs reduced by10%

comment.narrative: PDO indicators redefined. The increase in productivity measured by land and labor productivity (PDO Indicator 7)

title.narrative: Participatory M&E system integrated to MIS

comment.narrative: Replaced by Intermediate Outcome Indicator 15.
Replaced by Intermediate Outcome Indicator 17.
The indicator was dropped. COMRURAL, however, generated more than 2,100 new jobs, 24% of which were on permanent basis.

title.narrative: Rural producers participating in the project experience 20% increase in land and labor productivity

comment.narrative: Achieved. Land productivity increased by 21% among coffee RPO members and 33% among vegetables RPO members. Labor productivity increased by 23% for coffee and 20% for vegetables.

title.narrative: Compliance with Project Operational Manual, including Safeguards and Anti-Corruption policies

comment.narrative: Achieved
Achieved
Achieved. MIS was set up in 2015 and functioned since. The original indicator was clarified, which was "MIS in place and in function".

title.narrative: Baseline data in the MIS is available for each approved business plan

comment.narrative: Achieved. The original indicator was clarified, which was "Baseline surveys completed at department level".

Achieved. The project submitted independent financial audit reports, and the last report in 2015 was clean. The original indicator was revised, which was "Satisfactory technical and financial audits".

title.narrative: 80% of the investments identified in the business plans are completed on schedule

comment.narrative: Not achieved. This was due to change in activities affected by coffee rust as well as delay in procurement, particularly coffee post-harvest equipment (dryers, etc.), some of which had to be imported from Columbia or Europe.

title.narrative: At least 70% of business plans in the project successfully implemented measures that target the youth and indigenous communities, when applicable, as identified in the business plan

comment.narrative: Exceeded. As per the indigenous people's plan (IPP) and participation plan, the project ensured consultation and participation of indigenous and youth producers in business plan development and implementation. Almost 50% of RPO members were indigenous.

title.narrative: At least 70% of business plans in the project are implemented using good environmental practices, as proposed in the business plan

comment.narrative: Exceeded. The project identified good environmental practices for each targeted product and monitored their implementation. For instance, for coffee and vegetables, the project encouraged use of composting/vermiculture and soil analysis.
